finding.claim: Unvalidated iconUrl supplied via PUT /profile is fetched server-side with a GET in the nightly sync(), enabling blind SSRF to internal hosts (including IMDSv1 over HTTP). Response body is discarded, so the bug is blind.
finding.source: Profile.java:11 — `icon` parameter of update(String webhook, String icon), reachable via PUT /profile (line 10). Handler not in repo; reachability and auth assumed from the comment.

trace.note: icon enters update() as a raw string
this.iconUrl = icon; stored with no validation
sync(HttpClient c) runs as nightly job
URI.create(iconUrl) and GET sent with shared HttpClient
response body discarded via ofByteArray(); never returned or logged

finding.guards_checked: No validation of icon in update() (only webhook is checked at line 12). Scheme: java.net.http.HttpClient accepts only http/https, so file:/jar:/ftp: are blocked, but internal http is not. Redirects: HttpClient defaults to Redirect.NEVER; caller-supplied client config not visible. Destination: no host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP check, no DNS pinning, so hostnames resolving to 127.0.0.1, 10.x, or 169.254.169.254 are fetched. Not reported: webhookUrl (line 21) is gated by an anchored String.matches regex with a fixed host and a 20-alphanumeric path, so no userinfo/fragment/traversal/query and no arbitrary-host steering.

verdict.guard_found: none: no validation of `icon` in Profile.java:11-17 (only `webhook` is checked at line 12), and sync() at lines 20-25 applies no host, IP, or scheme check before URI.create(iconUrl) at line 23.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate and no closing guard exists (icon is stored unvalidated at Profile.java:16 and fetched at Profile.java:23-24), but the PUT /profile handler that feeds `icon` is not in the repo (the only match for "PUT" is the comment at Profile.java:10), so I cannot confirm that a low-privilege remote user can set iconUrl and the verdict cannot be CONFIRMED from this code alone.
